passages.text: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to speak first to His disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
passages.sermon:
A crowd of many thousands gathered.
The people in the crowd were so many that they trampled one another.
Jesus saw the crowd.
Jesus spoke first to His disciples.
Jesus warned His disciples.
He said, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.
The leaven of the Pharisees is hypocrisy.”
passages.original: Ἐν οἷς ἐπισυναχθεισῶν τῶν μυριάδων τοῦ ὄχλου ὥστε καταπατεῖν ἀλλήλους ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ πρῶτον Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης ἥτις ἐστὶν ὑπόκρισις τῶν Φαρισαίων

passages.text: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about the Pharisees’ hypocrisy.
He said, “Nothing is concealed that will not be revealed.
Nothing is hidden that will not become known.”
passages.original: οὐδὲν δὲ συγκεκαλυμμένον ἐστὶν ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται

passages.text: What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about hypocrisy.
He said, “What you say in the dark will be heard in the light.”
He said, “What you whisper in private rooms will be announced from the rooftops.”
passages.original: ἀνθ’ ὧν ὅσα ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ ἀκουσθήσεται καὶ ὃ πρὸς τὸ οὖς ἐλαλήσατε ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις κηρυχθήσεται ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων

passages.text: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His friends.\r\nHe said, “Do not be afraid of people who can kill your body.\r\nAfter they kill the body, they cannot do anything more to you.”
passages.original: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν τοῖς φίλοις μου μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεινόντων τὸ σῶμα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ ἐχόντων περισσότερόν τι ποιῆσαι

passages.text: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His friends.
He told them whom they should fear.
God has authority over life and death.
God can throw a person into hell after death.
Fear God.
Yes, I tell you, fear Him.
passages.original: ὑποδείξω δὲ ὑμῖν τίνα φοβηθῆτε φοβήθητε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποκτεῖναι ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν ἐμβαλεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν ναί λέγω ὑμῖν τοῦτον φοβήθητε

passages.text: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
passages.sermon: Five sparrows are sold for two pennies.\r\nGod does not forget any one of them.
passages.original: Οὐχὶ πέντε στρουθία πωλοῦνται ἀσσαρίων δύο καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπιλελησμένον ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
passages.sermon:
God knows you completely.
God counts every hair on your head.
God does not forget you.
Do not be afraid.
You are worth more than many sparrows.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν πᾶσαι ἠρίθμηνται μὴ φοβεῖσθε πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε

passages.text: I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus says this to the people.
Anyone confesses Jesus in front of other people.
The Son of Man will confess that person.
The Son of Man will do this in front of God’s angels.
passages.original: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν πᾶς ὃς ἂν ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁμολογήσει ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His followers.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
If anyone denies Jesus before other people, God will deny that person before His angels.
God’s angels are in His presence.
Denying Jesus before people leads to being denied before God’s angels.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ἀρνησάμενός με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρνηθήσεται ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
The Holy Spirit is God’s Spirit.
If anyone speaks against the Son of Man, God will forgive that person.
If anyone blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, God will not forgive that person.
passages.original: καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐρεῖ λόγον εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ δὲ εἰς τὸ Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα βλασφημήσαντι οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται

passages.text: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about future challenges.
People will bring you before synagogues.
People will bring you before rulers.
People will bring you before authorities.
Do not worry about how to defend yourselves.
Do not worry about what you should say.
passages.original: Ὅταν δὲ εἰσφέρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί ἀπολογήσησθε ἢ τί εἴπητε

passages.text: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.”
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit is God’s Spirit.
The Holy Spirit will help you.
The Holy Spirit will teach you.
The Holy Spirit will teach you at that very moment.
The Holy Spirit will show you what you must say.
passages.original: τὸ γὰρ Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα διδάξει ὑμᾶς ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἃ δεῖ εἰπεῖν

passages.text: Someone in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
passages.sermon:
A man stood in the crowd.
He spoke to Jesus.
He called Jesus “Teacher.”
He said, “Teacher, tell my brother to share the inheritance with me.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δέ τις ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε εἰπὲ τῷ ἀδελφῷ μου μερίσασθαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ τὴν κληρονομίαν

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the man in the crowd.\r\nJesus said, “Man, who made Me your judge?”\r\nJesus said, “Who made Me the one to divide things between you?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἄνθρωπε τίς με κατέστησεν κριτὴν ἢ μεριστὴν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς

passages.text: And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He warned them.
He said, "Be careful.
Protect yourselves from all kinds of greed.
A person's life does not depend on how many things he owns.
Having many possessions does not give true life."
passages.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Ὁρᾶτε καὶ φυλάσσεσθε ἀπὸ πάσης πλεονεξίας ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν τινὶ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ

passages.text: Then He told them a parable: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them a parable.
He said, “There was a rich man.
His land produced a large harvest.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα

passages.text: So he thought to himself, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’
passages.sermon:
A certain man was rich.
His land produced a large harvest.
He thought about his situation.
He said to himself, “What should I do?”
He had a problem.
He had no place to store his crops.
passages.original: καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων Τί ποιήσω ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου

passages.text: Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods.
passages.sermon:
The rich man spoke to himself.
He decided what to do.
He said, "I will tear down my barns."
"I will build bigger barns."
"I will store all my grain in the new barns."
"I will also store all my goods there."
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν Τοῦτο ποιήσω καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα τὸν σῖτον καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου

passages.text: Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!” ’
passages.sermon:
A rich man spoke to himself.
He said, “Self, you have many good things stored up.
You have enough for many years.
Rest now.
Eat.
Drink.
Be happy.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου Ψυχή ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά ἀναπαύου φάγε πίε εὐφραίνου

passages.text: But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the rich man.
God called him a fool.
God said, “Tonight your life will be taken from you.”
God asked, “Who will get what you have prepared?”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Θεός Ἄφρων ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας τίνι ἔσται

passages.text: This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about greed.
A person may store up treasure for himself.
He may gather many possessions.
He may not be rich toward God.
God does not value only earthly wealth.
A person who is not rich toward God will lose everything.
He cannot keep his treasures.
He will not have true riches with God.
passages.original: Οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς Θεὸν πλουτῶν

passages.text: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Do not worry about your life.
Do not worry about what you will eat.
Do not worry about your body.
Do not worry about what you will wear.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ τί φάγητε μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε

passages.text: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.
passages.sermon: Life is more important than food.\r\nThe body is more important than clothes.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος

passages.text: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them to look at the ravens.
Ravens do not plant seeds.
Ravens do not gather a harvest.
Ravens do not have a storehouse.
Ravens do not have a barn.
God gives food to the ravens.
You are much more valuable than birds.
God cares for you even more.
passages.original: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη καὶ ὁ Θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν

passages.text: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about worry.
He asked a question.
He said, “Can any one of you add time to your life by worrying?”
No one can make his life longer by worrying.
Worry does not give you more time.
passages.original: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι πῆχυν

passages.text: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?
passages.sermon:
You cannot do even a very small thing.
You cannot add a single hour to your life by worrying.
You cannot control the smallest matters by your own effort.
Why do you worry about other things?
Why do you let concern for the rest trouble you?
God cares for you.
Trust Him instead of worrying.
passages.original: εἰ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε

passages.text: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them to look at the lilies.
The lilies grow in the field.
The lilies do not work hard.
The lilies do not spin thread.
God makes the lilies beautiful.
Solomon was a great and rich king.
Solomon had much glory.
But even Solomon was not dressed as beautifully as one of these lilies.
passages.original: Κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς αὐξάνει οὐ κοπιᾷ οὐδὲ νήθει λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων

passages.text: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!
passages.sermon:
God cares for the grass in the field.
The grass lives today.
Tomorrow, people throw the grass into the furnace.
God clothes the grass with beauty.
You are more important than grass.
God will clothe you even more.
You have little faith.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἐν ἀγρῷ τὸν χόρτον ὄντα σήμερον καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ Θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέζει πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς ὀλιγόπιστοι

passages.text: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them not to worry about food.
He told them not to worry about drink.
He told them not to be anxious.
passages.original: Καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε καὶ τί πίητε καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε

passages.text: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
passages.sermon:
The Gentiles of the world seek these things.
They strive after food, drink, and clothing.
Your Father is God.
God knows that you need these things.
passages.original: ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ἐπιζητοῦσιν ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ Πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων

passages.text: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them what to do first.
Seek God's kingdom.
Do not focus on food or drink.
God will give you what you need.
If you seek His kingdom, God will add these things to you.
passages.original: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν

passages.text: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
\r\nHe called them a little flock.
\r\nHe told them not to be afraid.
\r\nGod is their Father.
\r\nGod is pleased.
\r\nGod wants to give them the kingdom.
passages.original: Μὴ φοβοῦ τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν

passages.text: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He told them to sell their possessions.
He told them to give to the poor.
He told them to provide purses for themselves that will not wear out.
He told them to store up a treasure in heaven that will never fail.
No thief can come near this treasure.
No moth can destroy this treasure.
passages.original: Πωλήσατε τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ὑμῶν καὶ δότε ἐλεημοσύνην ποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς βαλλάντια μὴ παλαιούμενα θησαυρὸν ἀνέκλειπτον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ὅπου κλέπτης οὐκ ἐγγίζει οὐδὲ σὴς διαφθείρει

passages.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
\r\nHe called them his little flock.
\r\nHe told them not to be afraid.
\r\nGod the Father is pleased to give them the kingdom.
\r\nJesus said, "Where your treasure is, your heart will be there also."
\r\nYour treasure is what you value most.
\r\nYour heart follows what you value.
\r\nIf you store treasure in heaven, your heart will be with God.
\r\nIf you store treasure on earth, your heart will be with earthly things.
passages.original: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρὸς ὑμῶν ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ καρδία ὑμῶν ἔσται

passages.text: Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He tells them to be ready for action.
He says, "Keep your clothes fastened for work."
He commands, "Keep your lamps burning."
He wants his followers to stay prepared and alert.
passages.original: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι

passages.text: Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He told them to be ready.
He said, "You must be like servants."
These servants wait for their master.
The master is away at a wedding banquet.
The servants do not know when he will return.
They watch and wait for him.
When the master comes back, he knocks at the door.
The servants are ready.
They open the door for him immediately.
passages.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He described faithful servants.
These servants stay alert and ready.
Their master returns and finds them watching.
These servants are blessed.
The master will prepare himself to serve them.
He will invite them to sit at the table.
He will come to them.
He will serve them himself.
passages.original: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples about servants waiting for their master.
The master may return late at night.
He may come during the second watch of the night.
He may come during the third watch of the night.
If the master finds the servants awake and ready, he will bless them.
Those servants will be blessed because they stayed alert.
passages.original: κἂν ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ κἂν ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως μακάριοί εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι

passages.text: But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about being ready.
He gave an example about a homeowner.
The homeowner owns a house.
A thief plans to come and break in.
If the homeowner knew the hour the thief would come, he would stay alert.
He would not allow his house to be broken into.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται οὐκ ἂν ἀφῆκεν διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to his disciples.
He calls himself the Son of Man.
You must be ready.
The Son of Man will come.
He will come at an hour you do not expect.
passages.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται

passages.text: “Lord,” said Peter, “are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter asked Jesus a question.
Peter said, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us?”
Peter also asked, “Or are you telling it to everyone?”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος Κύριε πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγεις ἢ καὶ πρὸς πάντας

passages.text: And the Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke.
He asked a question.
He said, "Who is the faithful manager?"
He said, "Who is the wise manager?"
A master chooses a manager.
The master puts this manager in charge of his servants.
The manager must give the servants their food at the right time.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Κύριος Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς οἰκονόμος ὁ φρόνιμος ὃν καταστήσει ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ διδόναι ἐν καιρῷ τὸ σιτομέτριον

passages.text: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He described a servant.
The servant obeys his master.
The servant does what the master commands.
The master returns.
The master finds the servant doing his duty.
That servant is blessed.
passages.original: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ποιοῦντα οὕτως

passages.text: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
Jesus described a faithful and wise servant.
The master finds this servant doing his duty.
The master trusts this servant.
The master puts this servant in charge of all his possessions.
This servant receives great responsibility.
passages.original: ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν

passages.text: But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master will be a long time in coming,’ and he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
passages.sermon:
A servant works for his master.
The servant thinks in his heart.
He says, “My master will take a long time to return.”
The servant begins to beat the male servants.
He also beats the female servants.
He eats a lot.
He drinks a lot.
He gets drunk.
passages.original: Ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἔρχεσθαι καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας ἐσθίειν τε καὶ πίνειν καὶ μεθύσκεσθαι

passages.text: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.
passages.sermon:
The master is the owner and authority over the servant.
The servant does not expect the master to come.
The master will come on a day the servant does not expect.
The master will come at an hour the servant does not anticipate.
The master will punish the servant severely.
The master will assign the servant a place with the unbelievers.
passages.original: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων θήσει

passages.text: That servant who knows his master’s will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.
passages.sermon:
A servant knows what his master wants.
This servant does not prepare.
This servant does not do what his master wants.
The master will punish this servant with many blows.
passages.original: Ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ὁ γνοὺς τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ ἑτοιμάσας ἢ ποιήσας πρὸς τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ δαρήσεται πολλάς

passages.text: But the one who unknowingly does things worthy of punishment will be beaten with few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from him who has been entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.
passages.sermon:
A person may do wrong things without knowing they are wrong.
This person will still be punished.
He will receive only a few blows.
God gives some people many gifts and responsibilities.
God will require much from everyone who receives much.
God will demand even more from anyone who is trusted with much.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ μὴ γνοὺς ποιήσας δὲ ἄξια πληγῶν δαρήσεται ὀλίγας παντὶ δὲ ᾧ ἐδόθη πολύ πολὺ ζητηθήσεται παρ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ᾧ παρέθεντο πολύ περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
passages.sermon: Jesus is speaking.\r\nJesus says, "I have come to bring fire to the earth."\r\nI desire that this fire is already burning.
passages.original: Πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη

passages.text: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus says he must undergo a baptism.
This baptism is not water baptism.
This baptism means great suffering and death.
Jesus feels deep distress.
He remains distressed until this suffering is finished.
passages.original: βάπτισμα δὲ ἔχω βαπτισθῆναι καὶ πῶς συνέχομαι ἕως ὅτου τελεσθῇ

passages.text: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, “Do you think I have come to bring peace to the earth?”
He answered, “No, I have not come to bring peace.”
He said, “I have come to bring division.”
passages.original: Δοκεῖτε ὅτι εἰρήνην παρεγενόμην δοῦναι ἐν τῇ γῇ οὐχί λέγω ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ἢ διαμερισμόν

passages.text: From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said what would happen because of his coming.
He said, “From now on, there will be division in families.”
In one household, there will be five people.
These five people will not be united.
Three will be against two.
Two will be against three.
They will be divided against each other.
passages.original: ἔσονται γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πέντε ἐν ἑνὶ οἴκῳ διαμεμερισμένοι τρεῖς ἐπὶ δυσὶν καὶ δύο ἐπὶ τρισίν

passages.text: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said that families will be divided.
A father will be against his son.
A son will be against his father.
A mother will be against her daughter.
A daughter will be against her mother.
A mother-in-law will be against her daughter-in-law.
A daughter-in-law will be against her mother-in-law.
passages.original: διαμερισθήσονται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί μήτηρ ἐπὶ τὴν θυγατέρα καὶ θυγάτηρ ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα πενθερὰ ἐπὶ τὴν νύμφην αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν πενθεράν

passages.text: Then Jesus said to the crowds, “As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds.
He said, "You see a cloud rise in the west.
You say, 'A shower is coming.'
Rain does come, just as you said."
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις Ὅταν ἴδητε τὴν νεφέλην ἀνατέλλουσαν ἐπὶ δυσμῶν εὐθέως λέγετε ὅτι Ὄμβρος ἔρχεται καὶ γίνεται οὕτως

passages.text: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds.
He described how people observe the weather.
When the south wind blows, you say, “It will be hot.”
And it becomes hot.
passages.original: καὶ ὅταν νότον πνέοντα λέγετε ὅτι Καύσων ἔσται καὶ γίνεται

passages.text: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds.
He called them hypocrites.
He said they know how to interpret the appearance of the earth.
He said they know how to interpret the appearance of the sky.
He asked why they do not know how to interpret the present time.
passages.original: ὑποκριταί τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γῆς καὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν τὸν καιρὸν δὲ τοῦτον πῶς οὐκ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν

passages.text: And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He called them hypocrites.
He said they could interpret the earth and sky.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Why do you not judge what is right for yourselves?”
passages.original: Τί δὲ καὶ ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν οὐ κρίνετε τὸ δίκαιον

passages.text: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them about dealing with an adversary.
If you are going with your adversary to the magistrate, act quickly.
Try hard to settle the matter with your adversary on the way.
If you do not, your adversary may take you to the judge.
The judge may hand you over to the officer.
The officer may put you in prison.
passages.original: ὡς γὰρ ὑπάγεις μετὰ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου σου ἐπ’ ἄρχοντα ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ δὸς ἐργασίαν ἀπηλλάχθαι ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μή‿ ποτε κατασύρῃ σε πρὸς τὸν κριτήν καὶ ὁ κριτής σε παραδώσει τῷ πράκτορι καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ σε βαλεῖ εἰς φυλακήν

passages.text: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He warned them about judgment.
He said, “You will not get out of prison.
You must pay the very last penny before you can leave.”
passages.original: λέγω σοι οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως καὶ τὸ ἔσχατον λεπτὸν ἀποδῷς
